layers.note: An open clump of hedgehog cactus stems among the shrubs.

moisture.note: Dry flats to steep canyon sides.

elevation_m.note: Mostly 600 to 1,000 m, at times to 1,500 m (Flora of North America).

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about 7 to 14 °C; gone below 4 °C and above 16 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −10 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −14 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 27 to 33 °C; gone below 24 °C, where summers are too short, and above 35 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 5,800 to 9,500 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 4,800.

degree_days_5.note: About 4,100 to 7,600 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 3,200.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.08 to 0.4, gone by 0.05 and above 0.5.

summer_rain.note: Needs the monsoon's summer rain: from about 0.3 of the year's precipitation in summer, gone below 0.25; up to about 0.7, gone by 0.8.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Saguaro desert scene (the west bajada of Saguaro National Park's Tucson Mountain District, about 750 m, 32.25 N 111.17 W) from general knowledge of the species and the ranges, habitats and elevations in the sources read for its spec (2026-10-19). Pinkflower hedgehog cactus grows in the Sonoran Desert, desert grassland and interior chaparral of central and southern Arizona and Sonora (Flora of North America). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records; every full range holds the bajada's climate (coldest month about 11 °C, warmest about 31 °C, about 7,600 degree-days above 0 °C, coldest night about −4 °C, moisture index about 0.15, about half the year's rain in summer).
